analysis: The supplied PR changes are documentation only: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/fused-causal-prefill-attention.md, lines 1-5) and one added row in docs/architecture/inference.md (head line 850). No source code (AttentionV1.swift, PagedLayerCache.swift) is in the supplied units, so the actual behavior of the fused causal prefill path was not reviewed. The docs describe a performance change: a single fused `.causal` attention call replaces 128-query blocks for full-attention prompt chunks on certain head_dims. Sliding-window, softcap, vision-span, bidirectional-mask and live packed paged KV paths are stated to be unchanged. Security-relevant observations: (1) The attention change alters only prefill compute/memory, and the docs claim peak memory drops. There is no stated change to encryption, attestation, authorization, cache scoping or at-rest artifacts, so T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier) and the cache salt scoping are not affected by what is visible. A faster cold prefill could marginally change the TTFT hit/miss gap, which falls under the already-accepted SEC-035 residual and is not a new class. (2) The new env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0 is an operator-local kill switch; the changelog notes the LaunchAgent does not receive it. This is a functional, not security, issue. (3) The changelog states that Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and other qualifying models were not measured, and that Qwen outputs on M5 can differ within bf16 rounding. That is a correctness and qualification caveat, and T-007 and T-056 already state that correct computation is not attested. The next pass should confirm in the actual Swift code that the fused path is bypassed for paged-KV masks, vision spans and cross-request packed rows, so no cross-request attention leakage occurs. Cross-tenant mask correctness for packed paged KV is not verifiable from docs alone, so I flag a deeper review of the code diff if it ships in another batch.
